observations: GPX4 mRNA was significantly upregulated in tumor tissues compared to adjacent nontumor tissues.
In a cohort of 365 HCC patients, those with the highest levels of GPX4 mRNA in their tumors experienced the poorest survival outcomes.
Genetic inhibition of GPX4 markedly suppressed the proliferation of Huh7 and SK-Hep1 cells.
40 positive and 113 negative regulators of GPX4 protein levels were identified.
MALT1-knockout PLC/PRF/5 cells exhibited significantly reduced GPX4 protein levels compared to control cells.
In Hep3B cells, MALT1-knockout cells showed a 40 to 50% reduction in GPX4 mRNA levels.
The reduction in GPX4 protein levels caused by MALT1-knockout could be mitigated by the proteasome inhibitor MG132.
The reduction in GPX4 protein levels caused by MALT1-knockout was enhanced by the protein synthesis inhibitor cycloheximide.
Elevated levels of GPX4 ubiquitination were observed in MALT1-knockout cells.
MALT1-knockout increased the susceptibility of liver cancer cells to ferroptosis induced by GPX4 inhibitors RSL3 or ML210.
A positive correlation between MALT1 and GPX4 protein levels was identified across CCLE pan-cancer cell lines.
A significant positive correlation between MALT1 and GPX4 protein levels was revealed in tissue array analysis of 75 human HCC tissues.

An increase in lipid ROS levels was noted in KTC-1, OSRC-2, and LoVo cells upon combination treatment.

Ferroptosis induction in vivo was evident in tumor tissues with combination treatment, as demonstrated by GPX4 and 4-HNE staining.
